questions.stem:
[In this question $\mathbf{i}$ and $\mathbf{j}$ are horizontal unit vectors due east and due north respectively and position vectors are given relative to a fixed origin $O$.]

Two cars $P$ and $Q$ are moving on straight horizontal roads with constant velocities. The velocity of $P$ is $(15\mathbf{i}+20\mathbf{j})\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ and the velocity of $Q$ is $(20\mathbf{i}-5\mathbf{j})\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find the direction of motion of $Q$, giving your answer as a bearing to the nearest degree.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: $\tan\theta = \frac{5}{20}$ (or $\pm\frac{5}{20}$ or $\pm\frac{20}{5}$, or any other complete method)
A1: $\theta = 14.04^\circ$ (or $\pm 75.96^\circ$)
A1: $104^\circ$ nearest degree
Official notes (completeness pass):
- Allow column vectors throughout

parts.label: b
parts.text:
At time $t=0$, the position vector of $P$ is $400\mathbf{i}$ metres and the position vector of $Q$ is $800\mathbf{j}$ metres. At time $t$ seconds, the position vectors of $P$ and $Q$ are $\mathbf{p}$ metres and $\mathbf{q}$ metres respectively.
(b) Find an expression for
(i) $\mathbf{p}$ in terms of $t$,
(ii) $\mathbf{q}$ in terms of $t$.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1 A1: $\mathbf{p} = 400\mathbf{i} + t(15\mathbf{i}+20\mathbf{j})$ (M1 for clear attempt at either $\mathbf{p}$ or $\mathbf{q}$; allow slip but $t$ must be attached to the velocity vector and position vector and velocity vector must be paired up correctly; "$\mathbf{p}=$" not needed but must be clear it's $P$)
A1: $\mathbf{q} = 800\mathbf{j} + t(20\mathbf{i}-5\mathbf{j})$ ("$\mathbf{q}=$" not needed but must be clear it's $Q$)

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) Find the position vector of $Q$ when $Q$ is due west of $P$.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: Equate their $\mathbf{j}$ components: $20t(\mathbf{j}) = (800-5t)(\mathbf{j})$ (allow $\mathbf{j}$'s on both sides)
A1: $t = 32$
M1 (independent): substituting their $t$ value into their $\mathbf{q}$ from (b)
A1: $\mathbf{s} = 800\mathbf{j} + 32(20\mathbf{i}-5\mathbf{j}) = 640\mathbf{i}+640\mathbf{j}$

parts.label: a
parts.text:
A vertical rope $AB$ has its end $B$ attached to the top of a scale pan. The scale pan has mass $0.5\,\mathrm{kg}$ and carries a brick of mass $1.5\,\mathrm{kg}$, as shown in Figure 1. The scale pan is raised vertically upwards with constant acceleration $0.5\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$ using the rope $AB$. The rope is modelled as a light inextensible string.
(a) Find the tension in the rope $AB$.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1 A1: $T - 0.5g - 1.5g = 2\times 0.5$ (M1 for an equation for whole system in $T$ only, with usual rules; A1 for a correct equation)
A1: $T = 20.6$ (N) or $21$ (N)
Official notes (completeness pass):
- N.B. In both parts of this question use the mass which is being used to guide you as to which part of the system is being considered

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Find the magnitude of the force exerted on the scale pan by the brick.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1 A1: $R - 1.5g = 1.5\times 0.5$ (M1 for an equation for the brick only (1st alternative) or for the scale pan only (2nd alternative), with usual rules; A1 for a correct equation, in the second alternative $T$ does not need to be substituted)
A1: Force $= 15.5$ (N) or $15$ (N)
OR: $T - R - 0.5g = 0.5\times 0.5$, Force $= 15.5$ (N) or $15$ (N)
N.B. If $R$ is replaced by $-R$ in either equation, can score M1A1. This would lead to $R=-15.5$ or $-15$. The second A1 can then only be scored if the candidate explains why the negative sign is being ignored.

questions.stem:
Two trains $M$ and $N$ are moving in the same direction along parallel straight horizontal tracks. At time $t=0$, $M$ overtakes $N$ whilst they are travelling with speeds $40\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ and $30\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ respectively. Train $M$ overtakes train $N$ as they pass a point $X$ at the side of the tracks.

After overtaking $N$, train $M$ maintains its speed of $40\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ for $T$ seconds and then decelerates uniformly, coming to rest next to a point $Y$ at the side of the tracks.

After being overtaken, train $N$ maintains its speed of $30\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ for $25\,\mathrm{s}$ and then decelerates uniformly, also coming to rest next to the point $Y$.

The times taken by the trains to travel between $X$ and $Y$ are the same.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Sketch, on the same diagram, the speed-time graphs for the motions of the two trains between $X$ and $Y$.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
B1: shape ($M$) — correct shape, must start and finish on the axes
B1: figs $(40,T)$ marked clearly and correctly (if delineators omitted B0)
B1: shape ($N$) — correct shape, must start and finish on the axes
B1: figs $(30,25)$ marked clearly and correctly (if delineators omitted B0)
N.B. If graphs do not cross and/or do not finish at the same point, max score is B1B1B0B1.
N.B. If graphs done on separate diagrams, mark each and award the higher mark, i.e. can score max 2/4 for part (a).

parts.label: b
parts.text:
Given that $XY = 975$ m,
(b) find the value of $T$.
(8)
parts.mark_scheme:
For $N$: $\frac{1}{2}(25+25+t).30=975$ OR $\frac{1}{2}(25+t_1).30=975$ — M1 A1
$t=15$ OR $t_1=40$ — DM1 A1
For $M$: $\frac{1}{2}(25+t+T).40=975$ OR $\frac{1}{2}(t_1+T).40=975$ — M1 A1
$T=8.75$ ($8\frac{3}{4}$ or $\frac{35}{4}$ oe) — DM1 A1
ALTERNATIVE: They may find $t$ or $t_1$, in terms of $T$, from their $(M)$ equation, and substitute for $t$ or $t_1$ in their $(N)$ equation, and then solve for $T$:
For $M$: $\frac{1}{2}(25+t+T).40=975$ OR $\frac{1}{2}(t_1+T).40=975$ — M1 A1
$t=(\frac{1950}{40}-25-T)$ OR $t_1=(\frac{1950}{40}-T)$ — DM1 A1
For $N$: $\frac{1}{2}(25+25+t).30=975$ OR $\frac{1}{2}(25+t_1).30=975$, sub for $t$ or $t_1$ — M1 A1
$T=8.75$ ($8\frac{3}{4}$ or $\frac{35}{4}$ oe) — DM1 A1
N.B. When attempting to find the area of a triangle, must see $\frac{1}{2}\times\ldots$ to be able to award an M mark, i.e. M0 if $\frac{1}{2}$ is missing. N.B. When attempting to find the area of a trapezium, must see something of the form $\frac{1}{2}\times(a+b)h$ to be able to award an M mark, i.e. M0 if $\frac{1}{2}$ is missing and bracket is not a sum. Any single suvat equation using $s=975$ is M0.
Official notes (completeness pass):
- First M1 for attempt at using 975m distance travelled by N to obtain an equation in one unknown time (usually extra time t after 25 s, but could, for example, be whole time $t_1$). They may use the area under their graph or use suvat (N.B. Any single suvat equn using s = 975 is M0). First A1 for a correct equation in their unknown time e.g. $(30 \times 25) + \frac{1}{2}30t = 975$ OR $(30 \times 25) + \frac{1}{2}30(t_1 - 25) = 975$. Second M1, dependent on first M, for solving their equation. Second A1 for a correct value for their unknown.
- Third M1 for attempt at using 975m distance travelled by M to obtain an equation in T and possibly one other unknown time (usually extra time t after 25 s, but could, for example, be whole time $t_1$). They may use the area under their graph or use suvat (N.B. Any suvat equn using s = 975 is M0)
- Third A1 for a correct equation in T and possibly their unknown. This A1 can be earned if they just have a letter for their unknown :- e.g. $40T + \frac{1}{2}40.(25 + t - T) = 975$ OR $40T + \frac{1}{2}40.(t_1 - T) = 975$ or for an incorrect numerical value in place of t or $t_1$. Fourth M1, dependent on first, second and third M's, for solving for T. Fourth A1 for 8.75 or 35/4 or any other equivalent

parts.text:
A particle $P$ of mass 2 kg is held at rest in equilibrium on a rough plane by a constant force of magnitude 40 N. The direction of the force is inclined to the plane at an angle of 30°. The plane is inclined to the horizontal at an angle of 20°, as shown in Figure 2. The line of action of the force lies in the vertical plane containing $P$ and a line of greatest slope of the plane. The coefficient of friction between $P$ and the plane is $\mu$.

Given that $P$ is on the point of sliding up the plane, find the value of $\mu$.
(10)
parts.mark_scheme:
B1: $\mu R$ seen or implied
M1 A2: $R = 2g\cos 20^\circ + 40\cos 60^\circ$ (M1 for resolving perpendicular to the plane with usual rules, must be using $2g$ with $20^\circ$ or $70^\circ$ and 40 with $30^\circ$ or $60^\circ$; A1A0 if one error)
M1 A2: $F = 40\cos 30^\circ - 2g\cos 70^\circ$ (M1 for resolving parallel to the plane with usual rules, must be using $2g$ with $20^\circ$ or $70^\circ$ and 40 with $30^\circ$ or $60^\circ$; A1A0 if one error)
M1: eliminating $R$ to produce an equation in $\mu$ only (independent). Does not need to be $\mu=\ldots$
M1: solving for $\mu$ (independent)
A1: $\mu = \frac{40\cos 30^\circ - 2g\cos 70^\circ}{2g\cos 20^\circ + 40\cos 60^\circ} = 0.73$ or $0.727$
N.B. They may choose to resolve in 2 other directions e.g. horizontally and vertically. N.B. If $F$ is replaced by $-F$ in the second equation, treat this as an error unless they subsequently explain that they have their $F$ acting in the wrong direction, in which case they could score full marks for the question.

questions.stem:
Two forces $\mathbf{F}_1$ and $\mathbf{F}_2$ act on a particle $P$.

The force $\mathbf{F}_1$ is given by $\mathbf{F}_1 = (-\mathbf{i}+2\mathbf{j})$ N and $\mathbf{F}_2$ acts in the direction of the vector $(\mathbf{i}+\mathbf{j})$.

Given that the resultant of $\mathbf{F}_1$ and $\mathbf{F}_2$ acts in the direction of the vector $(\mathbf{i}+3\mathbf{j})$,

parts.label: a
parts.mark_scheme:
B1: $\mathbf{F}_2 = k\mathbf{i}+k\mathbf{j}$ ($k\neq 1$) seen or implied in working, including for an incorrect final answer, with the wrong $k$ value.
M1: $(-1+a)\mathbf{i}+(2+b)\mathbf{j}$ — adding the 2 forces (for this M mark we only need $\mathbf{F}_2 = a\mathbf{i}+b\mathbf{j}$, with i's and j's collected, implied by later working, allow a slip) (M0 if $a$ and $b$ both assumed to be 1)
DM1 A1: $\frac{-1+a}{2+b}=\frac{1}{3}$ (dependent on first M1, for ratio of their components = 1/3 or 3/1, must be correct way up for the M mark; A1 for a correct equation which may involve two unknowns)
DM1 A1; A1: $a=b=k=2.5$; $\mathbf{F}_2 = 2.5\mathbf{i}+2.5\mathbf{j}$ (dependent on first and second M1, for solving for $k$ oe; A1 for a correct $k$ value; A1 for $2.5\mathbf{i}+2.5\mathbf{j}$)
ALTERNATIVE (LHS = p(i+3j)): B1: $\mathbf{F}_2=k\mathbf{i}+k\mathbf{j}$; M1 for LHS $(-1+a)\mathbf{i}+(2+b)\mathbf{j}=p(\mathbf{i}+3\mathbf{j})$; DM1 A1: $-1+a=p$, $2+b=3p$; DM1 A1; A1: $a=b=k=2.5$; $\mathbf{F}_2=2.5\mathbf{i}+2.5\mathbf{j}$
ALTERNATIVE using two simultaneous equations: B1 for $\mathbf{F}_2=k\mathbf{i}+k\mathbf{j}$ ($k\neq1$) seen or implied; M1 for adding the 2 forces with i's and j's collected (LHS of equation) (M0 if $a$ and $b$ both assumed to be 1) allow a slip; M1 dependent on first M1, for equating coeffs to produce two equations in 2 or 3 unknowns, must have $p$ and $3p$ (M0 if $p$ is assumed to be 1 or $k$); A1 for two correct equations; M1 dependent on first and second M1, for solving for $k$ oe; A1 for a correct $k$ value; A1 for $2.5\mathbf{i}+2.5\mathbf{j}$
ALTERNATIVE using magnitudes and directions: B1 for $\mathbf{F}_2=k\mathbf{i}+k\mathbf{j}$ seen or implied in working; M1 for a correct vector triangle (for this M mark we only need $\mathbf{F}_2=a\mathbf{i}+b\mathbf{j}$) (M0 if $a$ and $b$ both assumed to be 1 and/or longest side is assumed to be $\sqrt{10}$); M1 dependent on first M1, for using sine rule on vector triangle; A1 for a correct equation, $45^\circ$ may not appear exactly: $\frac{k\sqrt{2}}{\sin 45^\circ}=\frac{\sqrt{5}}{\sin(90^\circ-\alpha)}$, $\alpha=\arctan 2$; $2k=5$; M1 dependent on first and second M1, for solving for $k$ oe; A1 for a correct $k$ value; A1 for $2.5\mathbf{i}+2.5\mathbf{j}$

parts.label: b
parts.text:
The acceleration of $P$ is $(3\mathbf{i}+9\mathbf{j})\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$. At time $t=0$, the velocity of $P$ is $(3\mathbf{i}-22\mathbf{j})\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$.
(b) Find the speed of $P$ when $t=3$ seconds.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: use of $\mathbf{v}=\mathbf{u}+\mathbf{a}t$ with $t=3$
A1: $\mathbf{v} = 3\mathbf{i}-22\mathbf{j}+3(3\mathbf{i}+9\mathbf{j}) = 12\mathbf{i}+5\mathbf{j}$ seen or implied. However, if a wrong $\mathbf{v}$ is seen A0
M1: finding magnitude of their $\mathbf{v}$
A1 (cso): $|\mathbf{v}| = \sqrt{12^2+5^2}=13\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$
